title: ServerlessLLM: Low-Latency Serverless Inference for Large Language Models
technique: Loading-optimized checkpoint format + multi-tier (SSD/DRAM/GPU) loading, token-based live migration of inference, and startup-time-optimized (locality-aware) model scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: ServerlessLLM is designed to minimize the model startup latency.
startup-time-optimized model scheduling, which assesses the locality statuses of checkpoints on each server and schedules the model onto servers that minimize the time to start the inference

headline_claim.text: ServerlessLLM dramatically outperforms state-of-the-art serverless systems, reducing latency by 10 - 200X across various LLM inference workloads.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 8-11 (mean/ P99 / P95 latency vs RPS, models, datasets)
Fig 6-7 checkpoint loading GB/s per storage medium
§7.4: fraction of requests served within 300 s timeout (89% vs 26%)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Their performance is thus measured by both first-token latency (i.e., the time to return the first token) and per-token latency (i.e., the average time to generate a token).
metric_definitions.notes: background definition only; evaluation does not report per-token latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For all experiments (unless we indicate otherwise), we report the model startup latency, a critical metric for serverless inference scenarios. When migration or preemption is enabled, this latency is added with pause latency, accounting for the impacts of delays.
metric_definitions.notes: time to get a model loaded and ready (incl. queueing for GPU, download/load), plus pause latency from migration/preemption; excludes decoding time. This is the headline latency metric

slo_spec: No SLO targets; requests have a 300 s timeout (fraction completed reported)
load_regime: request-rate sweep (RPS 0.2-1.4) on traces modeled on Azure serverless trace (Gamma-distributed bursty), GSM8K and ShareGPT datasets
tradeoff_acknowledged: Live migration/preemption adds pause latency to the migrated inference (counted in latency); Shepherd* preemption causes longer latency; at high RPS (1.4) ServerlessLLM latency also grows due to GPU resource contention
hardware: 8x NVIDIA A5000 server (NVMe/SATA SSD RAID) and 4-server GPU cluster with 10 Gbps network
workloads: GSM8K, ShareGPT, Azure serverless trace for arrivals
extractor_notes: Not a token-level serving paper: optimizes cold-start/model startup latency, not TTFT/TBT/throughput of a warm model. Headline 'latency' = model startup latency (plus pause latency). Mapped to OTHER:model_startup_latency; TTFT entry in optimized_metrics is a loose alias because the paper elsewhere calls it first-token latency in its Ray Serve/KServe comparison (§7.5).
load_class_quote: request-rate sweep (RPS 0.2-1.4) on Gamma-distributed bursty traces modeled on the Azure serverless trace (§7)
repass_log: TTFT entry demoted: abstract 'reducing latency by 10-200X' result headline, no design statement (the design target is OTHER:model_startup_latency; first-token latency only appears in motivation)
UTIL entry demoted (where: motivation only): quote is serverless motivation ('To reduce GPU consumption...'), not a design statement of this method
two OTHER:model_startup_latency entries kept as design (§3 'designed to minimize the model startup latency'; startup-time-optimized scheduling)
